channel.title: Github on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in Github on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — October 5
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s weekly release note says this update improves cross-account and cross-environment use, while adding more control over agent access and work management. The excerpt also references GitHub Copilot Claude Haiku, but no further details are included.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.27.2 improves C++, Go, Rust, and JavaScript analysis
item.description:
CodeQL 2.27.2 is available with a new C++ regular-expression parser and analysis improvements for C++, Go, Rust, and JavaScript. The update applies to the static analysis engine used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: New organization billing options and controls
item.description:
GitHub added billing and license controls for Copilot code review at the organization level. Organization owners can now bill code review usage to the org for members with Copilot licenses and manage related controls.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Triage role users or higher can now archive pull requests
item.description:
GitHub now allows users with the triage role or higher to archive and unarchive pull requests. Before this change, only repository administrators could perform this action.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Screen readers can navigate timelines as lists
item.description:
GitHub issue and pull request timelines are now exposed to screen readers as lists. Assistive technology can announce the list structure, item count, and current position while users move through a timeline.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Draft pull requests count toward pull request limits
item.description:
GitHub now lets repository maintainers configure pull request limits so draft pull requests are counted too. Before this change, draft PRs were excluded from those limits.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Claude Haiku 5.5 in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Claude Haiku 5.5 is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub describes it as a lightweight model for fast, high-volume tasks such as subagents, quick edits, and terminal work.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Purpose-built model for leaked secret detection
item.description:
GitHub announced a new purpose-built, context-aware model for leaked secret detection as part of Secret Protection. It is intended to improve secret detection in code workflows, including those that involve AI agents.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot now generally available
item.description:
Local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot is now generally available. It is supported in GitHub Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app, and VS Code sessions using Agent Host.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Discover local models in GitHub Copilot CLI
item.description:
GitHub Copilot CLI version 1.0.94-0 adds a /model command so you can discover supported local models from within the CLI instead of leaving your workflow.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Update your IDE to restore agent activity in Copilot usage metrics
item.description:
GitHub says some Copilot usage metrics showed declining agent activity and agent lines of code even as overall usage increased because of an IDE-related issue. A fix is rolling out, and users should update their IDE to restore correct agent activity reporting.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Stacked pull requests generally available
item.description:
GitHub stacked pull requests are now generally available. The feature lets you split large changes into smaller, focused pull requests that can be reviewed independently and merged together.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Code scanning AI Scan enablement status in security overview
item.description:
GitHub added AI Scan for pull requests enablement status to the security overview coverage view for organizations and enterprises. The code scanning summary now indicates which repositories have AI Scan enabled or not enabled.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Secret scanning adds detectors for Lovable, Supabase, and more
item.description:
GitHub Secret Scanning added new detectors for secrets from Lovable Labs, Pydantic Services Inc., and Supabase. A new provider also joined the secret scanning partnership program.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Stateless GitHub App installation tokens rolled out
item.description:
GitHub has completed the staged rollout of the stateless GitHub App installation token format. By default, newly minted installation tokens now use the new format.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: API support and new default effort level
item.description:
GitHub Copilot code review can now be requested through both the REST and GraphQL APIs, and each request can specify an effort level. The default effort level has changed to Balanced.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations now expire
item.description:
Unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations now expire 48 hours after creation and can no longer authorize publishing. This reduces the risk of a repository or project name changing after the configuration is created.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: npm staged publishing now supports creating new packages
item.description:
npm staged publishing now supports creating new packages. You can create a new package with npm stage publish using either a local session or a granular access token, including a stage-only token.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Selected models in GitHub Copilot deprecated
item.description:
GitHub deprecated several Copilot models across all Copilot experiences on October 2, 2026. The change applies to Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: New fields for SecurityAdvisory GraphQL API
item.description:
GitHub added five new fields to the SecurityAdvisory GraphQL object, allowing more of the GitHub Advisory Database to be read directly through GraphQL instead of using the REST API. The changelog notes one of the new fields as cveId.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Confidential comments on repository security advisories
item.description:
GitHub now supports confidential comments on repository security advisories. These comments are visible only to users with write access to the repository, allowing private discussion of a report.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Repository security advisory comments API in public preview
item.description:
GitHub has added REST API support for reading, adding, and editing comments on repository security advisories. The API also works for advisories created from private vulnerability reports.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Rate limits for private vulnerability reports
item.description:
GitHub is adding rate limits for private vulnerability reports to reduce low-quality and automated submissions that can obscure important reports. The change caps how many new reports a single account can submit.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Structured forms for private vulnerability reports
item.description:
Private vulnerability reports now support structured forms to collect the details needed for triage, including a reproducible proof of concept. This replaces reliance on a single free-text field with a more guided intake flow.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot can now interact with desktop apps with computer use
item.description:
GitHub Copilot computer use is now in public preview in Copilot CLI and the Copilot app on macOS and Windows. It can interact with desktop applications on the user’s behalf.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Actions: macOS 14 runner image retirement
item.description:
GitHub Actions will retire the macOS 14 runner image on November 2, 2026. Before removal, jobs that use macOS 14 will temporarily fail during scheduled awareness periods.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in VS Code, September 2026 releases
item.description:
September 2026 GitHub Copilot in VS Code releases cover VS Code v1.136 through v1.140 and focus on streamlining agent-driven development from implementation through pull request merge. The update adds automations for repeatable tasks and agent merge support.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Accessibility statements highlighted on repository overview
item.description:
GitHub now highlights an ACCESSIBILITY.md file on the repository overview when it is located in the repository root, .github/, or docs/. The changelog entry also notes support for adding or proposing an accessibility statement file.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Actions retention now covers checks, runs, and statuses
item.description:
GitHub Actions retention now applies to checks, workflow runs, and statuses, using the same retention setting that already controls artifacts and logs. This means those records are now kept or removed according to the repository or organization Actions retention policy.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Scheduled code scanning skips inactive repositories
item.description:
Weekly scheduled scans for code scanning default setup and GitHub Code Quality now run only after a repository has had an analysis triggered by a push or pull request. Repositories with no recent activity no longer count toward scheduled scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Code coverage uploads no longer fail CI for new branches
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality’s upload-code-coverage action no longer causes CI failures when coverage is uploaded from a branch that does not yet have an open pull request. This changes behavior from the previous failure case for new branches.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Dynamic workflows in Copilot CLI and the Copilot app
item.description:
Dynamic workflows are now available in Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app, and the GitHub Copilot SDK. They let you define an orchestration in code.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Opt-in dist-tag permissions for npm trusted publishing
item.description:
npm trusted publishing can now optionally get permission to manage dist-tags using short-lived OIDC credentials. This covers actions like moving tags such as latest, next, and beta without using long-lived credentials.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Advanced Security trials for GitHub Team
item.description:
GitHub Team customers can now start self-serve trials of GitHub Advanced Security from an organization’s Overview page and Billing settings. The trial lets teams evaluate GitHub Code Security and GitHub Secret Protection.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: HydraFusion in VS Code and the GitHub Copilot app
item.description:
HydraFusion research preview is now available in Visual Studio Code and the GitHub Copilot app, expanding access beyond Copilot CLI. It appears in the model picker in both products.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: X25519-only TLS ends for GHE.com on October 7
item.description:
Starting October 7, 2026, GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (GHE.com) will stop accepting TLS connections from clients that support only X25519 for key agreement. Most customers are not expected to be affected.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Repository custom runner settings for Dependabot
item.description:
Repository administrators can now set the runner type, optional custom label, and optional runner group for Dependabot version and security updates. This extends existing runner configuration options for Dependabot.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Bring business context with external custom properties
item.description:
GitHub now supports external custom properties so repository business context can be synced from a system of record such as a CMDB, internal developer portal, or other in-house system. This lets teams attach external metadata to repositories more seamlessly.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GPT-6.1 Sol in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GPT-6.1 Sol is now generally available and rolling out in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says it can be used for agentic coding and terminal workflows with strong multistep performance.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Self-hosted runner version enforcement date has moved
item.description:
GitHub has moved the enforcement date for minimum version requirements on self-hosted runners in GitHub Actions for GitHub Enterprise Cloud. The change ships on Monday, September 28, 2026, with full enforcement starting after that date.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Claude Sonnet 5.5 in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Claude Sonnet 5.5 is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says it is intended for well-scoped everyday tasks such as building features and fixing bugs.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise managed settings in-product validator
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now includes an in-product validator for enterprise managed settings. It checks for malformed JSON, unsupported configurations, invalid team mappings, and similar issues that could block settings from working correctly.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Usage metrics API adds pull request review stages
item.description:
GitHub’s enterprise and organization repository-level Copilot usage metrics reports now include pull request review stage timing. Each repos-1-day row gets a new pull_request_review_times array with time spent in each review stage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Private saved views for repository issues and “Relates to” issue relationship is generally available
item.description:
GitHub repository issues now support private saved views, allowing users to save personalized issue filters and layouts. The “Relates to” issue relationship is also generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Changes to query results in the GitHub Actions API and UI
item.description:
GitHub Actions workflow run queries in the API and UI now return a less precise but more accurate total count for search results across filters like workflow, event, status, and branch.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Agentic autofix now uses Copilot Memory
item.description:
Agentic autofix now checks Copilot Memory when that feature is enabled, using existing memories as context to help resolve security alerts.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — September 21
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s weekly release roundup adds new models, local sandboxing in the Copilot app, and updates across Copilot integrations in Slack, Microsoft Teams, JetBrains, and VS Code.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Updates to GitHub Copilot for Slack and Microsoft Teams
item.description:
GitHub Copilot in Slack and Microsoft Teams has been updated to provide more context, more control, and a clearer path from chat conversations to GitHub work. The changelog does not include specific feature details in the provided text.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.27.1 adds C and C++ query and Kotlin 2.4.20 support
item.description:
CodeQL 2.27.1 adds new queries for C/C++ and C#, support for Kotlin 2.4.20, and query-accuracy improvements. It is the static analysis engine used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Default Enablement of Copilot Features for Copilot Business and Enterprise
item.description:
GitHub is introducing a global default policy that enables generally available Copilot features and supported client capabilities in enterprise and organization Copilot settings. The change takes effect over a 28-day window.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Require proof of presence for high-impact actions
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Cloud now supports requiring proof of presence before members perform high-impact actions. This adds an interactive re-authentication or MFA challenge on top of the existing sudo-style control.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: More ways to request and configure Copilot code reviews
item.description:
GitHub Copilot code review now supports more personal configuration options, is available to a broader set of Copilot plans, and adds an enterprise-level default setting. These changes are generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Node 20 is no longer available in GitHub Actions
item.description:
GitHub Actions runners no longer include Node 20. JavaScript actions now run on Node 24, and the temporary ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION opt-out is no longer available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Local sandboxing in the GitHub Copilot app
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app now supports local sandboxing to limit the impact of unintended commands by restricting access to local files, network resources, and credentials. The feature is configured in the app.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: OpenTelemetry in the GitHub Copilot app
item.description:
The GitHub Copilot app now supports OpenTelemetry configuration via enterprise-managed settings. This lets organizations observe Copilot agent performance and interactions with models and tools.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: New features and improvements in Copilot for JetBrains
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains 1.18.0 adds AI-assisted tool approvals, more control over agent conversations, and organization-wide shared skills and instructions. It also includes plan review support with Codex.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Faster C++ code intelligence with whole codebase indexing
item.description:
GitHub Copilot CLI now supports whole-codebase indexing for C++ repositories, improving code intelligence performance. The change is aimed at large C++ codebases with many interconnected files.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Claude Opus 5.5 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Claude Opus 5.5 is now available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says it can be used for agentic coding, long-running agentic tasks, and knowledge work.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna now available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now includes two additional OpenAI GPT-6 models: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. They join the previously available GPT-6 Astra as selectable model options.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Security improvements for SSH
item.description:
GitHub is updating SSH security by removing several older algorithms, adding a new one, and requiring larger RSA SSH keys. The change tightens supported SSH configurations to improve security.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Deprecation notice: All-platform CodeQL bundle
item.description:
GitHub has deprecated the all-platform CodeQL bundle starting with CodeQL CLI 2.27.0. The deprecated artifacts are codeql-bundle.tar.gz and codeql-bundle.tar.zst, which previously included binaries for all supported platforms.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Refreshed repository pull requests page generally available
item.description:
GitHub has generally available a refreshed repository pull requests page for all users. The update is intended to make pull requests easier to find and act on from one place.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Enterprise adds credential inventory exports
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise now lets enterprise owners export a complete inventory of credentials that can access the enterprise. The export includes SSH keys, classic and fine-grained personal access tokens, OAuth App access tokens, and other credential types.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Grok 4.7 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Grok 4.7 is rolling out in GitHub Copilot. GitHub describes it as xAI’s latest reasoning model, intended for agentic coding and complex multistep workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: An improved review experience
item.description:
GitHub updated Copilot code review to make review changes easier to track over time, auto-resolve more of its own suggestions, and generate commit messages when suggestions are accepted.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Manage the code coverage ruleset condition with the REST API
item.description:
GitHub now supports managing the “Restrict code coverage” repository ruleset option through the generally available REST API, in addition to the existing UI. This lets admins enforce code coverage requirements programmatically.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — September 14
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s weekly release adds new model selection options, updates to code review, and Sentry integration in the Copilot app. The post also mentions additional admin updates and new agent features.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models in mid-October
item.description:
GitHub will deprecate selected Copilot models across all Copilot experiences on October 19, 2026. The affected models include those used in Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Stage-only npm tokens for safer automation
item.description:
GitHub added a new npm granular access token permission option, Read and write (stage only). It allows automated workflows to stage package versions for review without granting the token full publish access.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot impact dashboard now shows feature engagement
item.description:
The Copilot impact dashboard now includes feature engagement data, showing how many active users regularly use key Copilot features. Enterprise administrators can use it to identify widely adopted experiences and those that may need more attention.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Agentic CLI customizations now in the usage metrics API
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s usage metrics API now includes agentic CLI activity for skills, custom agents, MCP servers, slash commands, and plugins. This extends existing CLI report coverage with additional customization metrics.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Ubuntu 26 generally available and latest migration
item.description:
Ubuntu 26.04 runner images for GitHub Actions are now generally available and fully supported for production workflows on x64 and arm64. The release notes also mention a migration update.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Workflow execution protections in GitHub Actions generally available
item.description:
Workflow execution protections in GitHub Actions are now generally available for GitHub Enterprise, organizations, and repositories. The feature lets you define an allowlist to control who can execute workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Automate SSO authorization for classic PATs and SSH keys
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Cloud now lets enterprise admins automate SSO authorization for existing classic PATs and SSH keys across organizations, removing the need for developers to authorize each org manually.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: SCIM user responses now include a profileUrl attribute
item.description:
GitHub SCIM user responses now include the RFC 7643 standard profileUrl attribute. It returns the absolute URL of the GitHub account linked to the external identity.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot budget increase requests are generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now supports a request flow for users who have exhausted their AI credits, allowing them to ask for a budget increase instead of being fully blocked from credit-consuming features. The feature is now generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Code scanning AI Scan no longer requires CodeQL default setup
item.description:
AI Scan for pull requests can now find security vulnerabilities even when CodeQL default setup is not enabled on a repository. Previously, AI Scan for pull requests required CodeQL default setup.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enforce GitHub Advanced Security configurations
item.description:
Enterprise administrators can now enforce GitHub Advanced Security configurations at the enterprise level. This blocks organization and repository administrators from changing those settings.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot suggests custom properties definitions
item.description:
GitHub Copilot can now suggest allowed values when creating custom properties for repositories in an organization. The feature is in public preview for GitHub Copilot Business and Copilot users.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: SHA-1 in HTTPS on GitHub sunset
item.description:
GitHub has completed the scheduled sunset of SHA-1 for HTTPS on github.com and partner services. SHA-1 is now disabled for HTTPS connections.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Configure cost and quality in Copilot auto model selection
item.description:
GitHub Copilot auto model selection now has three tiers: efficiency, balance, and intelligence. These let you choose how auto weighs cost, quality, and response time.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Profiles now show your highest achievement badge tier
item.description:
GitHub profiles now display the highest tier earned for achievements that have multiple levels. Before this change, profiles could show the first tier earned even after a user progressed further.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Add VS Code Agents to Copilot usage metrics
item.description:
GitHub Copilot usage metrics now include generally available activity metrics for the dedicated VS Code Agents window. This lets enterprises and organizations track adoption and engagement for VS Code Agents alongside other Copilot usage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Auto-resolution and analysis updates in Copilot code review
item.description:
Copilot code review now auto-resolves its own comments after you address them, and it can generate commit messages when you apply its code suggestions. The update also includes behind-the-scenes analysis changes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — September 7
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s Sept. 7 weekly release adds Jira integration in Copilot app and adaptive model orchestration via Project HydraFusion in Copilot CLI. It also introduces new agent automation in Visual Studio Code.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Refreshed repository pull requests page in public preview
item.description:
GitHub is previewing a refreshed repository-level pull request listing page for all users. The update adds stronger filtering and a compact presentation mode.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: AI Scan for pull request APIs in public preview
item.description:
GitHub code scanning’s AI Scan for pull request feature can now be enabled and managed via REST API at both the organization and repository levels. The APIs are in public preview.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Control GitHub Actions cache access with cache-mode
item.description:
GitHub Actions now supports cache-mode to control cache access at the workflow or job level. This lets you grant least-privilege cache access instead of broad cache permissions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: MAI-Code-1-Flash deprecated
item.description:
GitHub deprecated MAI-Code-1-Flash across all Copilot experiences on September 10, 2026. The suggested alternative is referenced in the deprecation notice.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Xcode 27 runner image now runs on macOS 27
item.description:
GitHub’s Xcode 27 runner image for GitHub-hosted macOS runners now runs on macOS 27 and is available in public preview. This lets you validate Apple apps against macOS 27 using that runner image.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: npm extends recovery-code security holds to all accounts
item.description:
npm now applies a 72-hour security hold to any account after a successful recovery-code sign-in. The hold was previously limited to high-impact accounts.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.27.0 adds support for Linux ARM64
item.description:
CodeQL 2.27.0 is available on Linux ARM64. The release also adds a new Rust security query, expands framework coverage for Java/Kotlin and C#, and includes analysis accuracy improvements across multiple languages.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise managed permissions for GitHub Copilot agent operations
item.description:
GitHub Copilot Business and Enterprise admins can now centrally manage agent operation permissions. Admins can set operations to be blocked, require human approval, or run without prompting.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Advanced Security expands trial availability
item.description:
GitHub Advanced Security self-serve trials are now available to more GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers. The trial can be used to evaluate GitHub Code Security and GitHub Secret Protection.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Block pull requests with exposed secrets from merging
item.description:
GitHub added a repository ruleset capability to prevent pull requests from merging when they introduce exposed secrets. This extends rulesets as a repository-wide protection mechanism.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Remediate Code Quality findings with agentic autofix
item.description:
GitHub added agentic autofix for Code Quality findings, allowing users to select and assign up to 25 standard findings at once for automated remediation. The feature is aimed at reducing backlog items in code quality reports.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise-managed sandbox in Copilot for JetBrains
item.description:
Copilot for JetBrains now supports enterprise-managed sandbox policies, along with cross-file cursor jumps for next edit suggestions, global project context in chat, and enterprise policy diagnostics. The update also adds a new terminal Copilot connection.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22 is now generally available
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22 is generally available. The release adds new platform capabilities, including administrator configuration for Copilot CLI.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: New customer portal help.github.com
item.description:
GitHub moved and redesigned its support portal to help.github.com. The new portal combines support, documentation, learning, community, account resources, and Copilot-powered search in one place.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 31
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s latest weekly release adds more model choice and content protection controls. VS Code also gets new options for managing agent sessions and preparing pull requests for merge.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GPT-6 Astra is generally available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GPT-6 Astra from OpenAI is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says the model is intended for long-horizon, autonomous coding and agentic tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: New API endpoint provides privacy-safe star history data
item.description:
GitHub added a new REST API endpoint for repository star history that lets users track star growth over time without exposing individual stargazer identities. This follows earlier restrictions on stargazer listing endpoints to admins and collaborators.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Multiple trusted publishing configurations for npm
item.description:
GitHub says three npm publishing updates are now generally available, including support for multiple trusted publishing configurations per package. The post also mentions staged publishing and another publishing-related change, but the provided excerpt does not include the full details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Actions: Early September 2026 updates
item.description:
GitHub Actions added three updates focused on workflow visibility and control. The post highlights a new REST API for runner version deprecations, but the provided excerpt does not include the full details of the other changes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models
item.description:
GitHub will deprecate selected Copilot models across all Copilot experiences on October 2, 2026. The affected models include Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub CLI Linux package signing key expires September 5
item.description:
The GitHub CLI Linux package repository signing key expires on September 5, 2026. After that date, repository metadata in APT and RPM workflows will be affected starting with the first release published after expiration.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Gemini 3.8 Flash is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now supports Gemini 3.8 Flash, Google’s latest Flash model. GitHub says early testing showed strong performance on complex terminal-based coding tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Reopening Copilot Business and Enterprise signups
item.description:
GitHub is gradually reopening sign-ups for Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise for customers paying by credit card or PayPal over the next few weeks. Availability is rolling out gradually to people who have been waiting to start.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.26.4 improves GitHub actions security detections
item.description:
CodeQL 2.26.4 is a new release that adds support for Go 1.27 and improves GitHub Actions security detections. It is part of the static analysis engine used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise-managed settings support any default model
item.description:
Enterprise-managed settings can now set any supported GitHub Copilot model as the default for new conversations. This lets enterprises choose the default model that best matches their workflow.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Content exclusions generally available in Copilot app and CLI
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app and CLI now honor content exclusion policies set at the enterprise, organization, and repository levels. Excluded files will not be used as context by Copilot.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise Live Migrations from GHES to ghe.com generally available
item.description:
Enterprise Live Migrations is now generally available for near-zero-downtime repository migrations from GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) to GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Data Residency (GHEC DR).

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Set an expiration date for individual user budgets
item.description:
GitHub now lets you set an optional expiration date on an individual user budget. When the date is reached, GitHub automatically removes the budget; the feature is generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review can now approve pull requests
item.description:
Copilot code review can now indicate when a pull request is ready for approval, and repository admins can authorize it to approve the PR. The approval capability is disabled by default.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Block users from discussion comments in personal repositories
item.description:
GitHub added in-context blocking controls for discussion comments in repositories owned by personal accounts. Users can now block or unblock other users directly from discussion comments, matching the existing issue and pull request comment behavior.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Claude Fable 5.1 is generally available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Claude Fable 5.1 from Anthropic is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says it is intended for long-horizon, autonomous coding and knowledge-work tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub CLI: Media in issues, pull requests, and comments
item.description:
GitHub CLI now supports a repeatable --attach flag to upload local images or videos and insert them inline in issue, pull request, or comment bodies. This adds media attachment support to GitHub CLI posts and comments.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot model access update for GitHub Team plans
item.description:
GitHub updated how Copilot model access is determined for users with seats in more than one organization. The change is intended to keep billing and governance aligned.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Selected GitHub Copilot models deprecated
item.description:
GitHub has deprecated selected Copilot models across most Copilot experiences, including Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions, effective September 1, 2026. The post notes that the affected models are no longer available in those experiences.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in VS Code, August 2026 releases
item.description:
VS Code v1.132 through v1.135, released in August 2026, add improvements to GitHub Copilot workflows focused on organizing agent sessions, reviewing changes, and navigating longer conversations. The changelog also mentions updates to Agent Host, but the provided excerpt does not include the details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — August update
item.description:
GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio’s August 2026 update adds more control over Copilot reasoning, model selection, sharing specialized agents within teams, and timing code review requests. The post is a high-level changelog summary rather than a detailed feature list.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 24
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s August 24 weekly release notes highlight more control over Copilot behavior across Slack, Teams, the app, CLI, and IDEs. The post mentions team sessions in Slack and Teams plus broader customization options, but the provided excerpt does not include specific feature details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming changes to GitHub Copilot policies and billing
item.description:
GitHub says three upcoming changes are coming to Copilot policies and billing. The post is a notice to review the updates, but the provided excerpt does not include the actual policy or billing details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Better label management on issues is generally available
item.description:
GitHub says improved label management for issues is now generally available. The update is aimed at making labels easier to organize and find in repositories with large or growing label lists.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: Resolution reasons and expanded capabilities
item.description:
Copilot code review now supports two additional pull request types: PRs authored by bots (including Copilot cloud agent) and very large pull requests. GitHub also added resolution reasons for code review outcomes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Classroom deprecated
item.description:
GitHub Classroom was deprecated on August 28, 2026 and replaced by selected partner solutions. The Classroom website, APIs, and related services have been decommissioned.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Actions retention will cover checks, workflow runs, and statuses
item.description:
Starting October 1, 2026, GitHub Actions retention settings will also apply to checks, workflow runs, and statuses, in addition to artifacts and logs. These data types will follow the same retention policy going forward.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Close all open contributions authored by a blocked user
item.description:
GitHub added an option to automatically close all open issues, discussions, and pull requests from a user when you block them from a personal account or organization. This applies to contributions authored by the blocked user at the time the block is set.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise-managed settings now support autoUpdate for plugin marketplaces
item.description:
Enterprise-managed settings now let admins enable automatic updates for specific plugin marketplaces by setting autoUpdate: true on an extraKnownMarketplaces entry. Supported clients will check the marketplace and update it automatically.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Global model policy generally available
item.description:
GitHub is gradually rolling out enforcement of a default global model policy for generally available GitHub Copilot models on Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise plans. The policy was announced in July and is now generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Apps can now access enterprise billing data
item.description:
GitHub Apps can now be granted access to enterprise billing data by enterprise owners. The app configuration flow now includes an enterprise billing permission that can be selected when creating or updating an app.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Rule insights dashboard generally available
item.description:
The rule insights dashboard is now generally available for both repositories and organizations. It provides a visual, high-level view of how GitHub evaluates and enforces repository rules.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot app Customize tab is generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s new Customize tab in the Copilot app is now generally available. It is meant to connect Copilot with a team’s existing tools, knowledge, and workflows, including MCP.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Block users directly from security advisories
item.description:
GitHub now lets repository owners block a user directly from a security advisory page in public repositories. The feature is available for repositories owned by organizations or personal accounts.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Push rules in rulesets now support path exceptions
item.description:
Push rules in GitHub rulesets now support path exceptions, letting you exempt specific file paths so a rule applies everywhere else in scope. The feature is available in public preview.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Better tools for managing blocked users
item.description:
GitHub updated blocked-user management for personal accounts and organizations. The blocked users list now supports search, sorting, and pagination to make large lists easier to manage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: The new GitHub Copilot experience in Slack
item.description:
GitHub’s Slack integration now includes agentic GitHub Copilot capabilities from Copilot CLI and the Copilot app, available in public preview. Users can interact with @GitHub in Slack to work with these features.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Shared agentic work with GitHub Copilot in Microsoft Teams
item.description:
GitHub Copilot can now be started from Microsoft Teams by mentioning @GitHub in a channel, thread, or direct message. This creates a shared agent session that participants can view and help guide.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Pinning saved views to the repository issues sidebar is generally available and more
item.description:
GitHub now lets you pin saved views to a repository’s issues sidebar, so frequently used views are easier to access. The feature is generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Windows 11 arm64 VS2026 image generally available
item.description:
Windows 11 arm64 images with Visual Studio 2026 are now generally available on standard and larger GitHub-hosted runners. Workflows can use the new image by updating the runner image reference.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Code scanning adds a mitigated alert dismissal reason
item.description:
Code scanning now supports dismissing alerts with the reason “Mitigated” when the vulnerability still exists in code but is offset by external controls, such as a web application firewall or network protections.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Separate GitHub Actions path for GitHub Code Quality
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality CodeQL Actions workflows now have a dedicated workflow path and are generally available. Run history and Actions usage reports can now distinguish GitHub Code Quality runs from other Actions workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Track GitHub Code Quality enablement changes in the audit log
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality now emits audit log events when it is enabled, disabled, or its repository settings are changed. This adds a history trail for Code Quality configuration changes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.26.3 improves GitHub Actions queries and JavaScript modeling
item.description:
CodeQL 2.26.3 adds source modeling for JavaScript, TypeScript, and Vue, and updates several GitHub Actions queries for better accuracy. It is a CodeQL release used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Track organization code quality trends
item.description:
GitHub’s organization-level Code Quality dashboard now has a Trends tab. It shows code quality changes across repositories over time instead of only a point-in-time view.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise managed settings in GitHub Copilot for JetBrains
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains now supports enterprise managed settings. Administrators can centrally control plugin governance, MCP server access, OpenTelemetry, and permission modes across the enterprise.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Credential revocation and deauthorization by token type
item.description:
GitHub added self-service incident response actions to deauthorize and revoke user credentials by token type and by specific user. The update extends existing credential revocation workflows for security incidents.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Multiple redirect URIs and token refresh for OAuth apps
item.description:
GitHub updated OAuth app and GitHub App platform support to improve app security. The changes include optional expiring access tokens with refresh tokens for OAuth apps, and support for multiple redirect URIs.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Grok 4.6 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Grok 4.6 is now rolling out in GitHub Copilot as a new reasoning model from xAI. GitHub says it is intended for agentic coding and complex multi-step workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 10
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s August 10 weekly release adds new models, portable plugins, and workflow improvements for agents. The updates are aimed at making Copilot more flexible across editors, the command line, and the Copilot app.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: License data quality improvements
item.description:
GitHub now sources license information for dependency graph software components from package registries such as npmjs.org and PyPI. This is intended to improve the accuracy and completeness of displayed license data.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Block users from comments in personal repositories
item.description:
GitHub now lets you block or unblock users directly from comments on pull requests and issues in repositories owned by personal accounts. The action can be performed from the comment interface.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Gemini 3.7 Flash is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot is rolling out Gemini 3.7 Flash, Google’s latest Flash model. GitHub says early testing showed improvements in web and app development and agentic tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Agent Plugins 1.0 in VS Code, Copilot CLI, and the Copilot app
item.description:
GitHub published Agent Plugins 1.0, enabling a plugin to be built once and used across compatible agent clients. The release is available in VS Code, Copilot CLI, and the Copilot app, with support announced alongside AWS, Anysphere, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Vercel.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Rule insights for organizations in public preview
item.description:
GitHub has released the rule insights dashboard in public preview for organizations. It provides a visual overview of how repository rulesets are evaluated and enforced at the organization level.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22 release candidate
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22 release candidate is now available. The post says it introduces new platform capabilities, with one highlighted change being administrator configuration for Copilot CLI.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot memory and Ollama in GitHub Copilot for JetBrains
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains adds persistent memory, local model access via Ollama, and additional enterprise controls. The update also improves chat workflows and fixes reliability issues with MCP servers.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Automatically migrate branch protection rules to repository rulesets
item.description:
GitHub now lets you convert existing branch protection rules into repository rulesets from repository settings. This provides a direct migration path to the newer policy framework.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of MAI-Code-1-Flash

GitHub will deprecate MAI-Code-1-Flash across all GitHub Copilot experiences on September 10, 2026. The suggested replacement is MAI-Code-1.1-Flash.

item.description:
MAI-Code-1.1-Flash is rolling out in GitHub Copilot. It adds native vision support for image understanding and improves coding quality over MAI-Code-1-Flash.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Per-model token breakdown in the usage report
item.description:
GitHub’s usage report now includes a per-model breakdown of tokens behind AI credits. The report shows token details for each model, including input, output, and cache usage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot on web expands conversation controls
item.description:
GitHub updated Copilot Chat on github.com with new conversation controls to make the web experience easier to use. The changes include quicker access to recent chats and the ability to minimize the chat panel.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub billing in India now supports automatic recurring payments

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Custom thread subscriptions are being deprecated

GitHub is deprecating custom thread subscription settings for notifications. Users will no longer be able to configure them, and support for existing custom thread subscription settings will be removed.

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 3
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s August 3 weekly release notes mention updates across the desktop app, CLI, and VS Code focused on resuming and organizing work, reviewing changes, and asking questions without losing context. The provided excerpt does not include the specific feature details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprises can now install third-party GitHub Apps
item.description:
Enterprise owners can now install public GitHub Apps built outside their enterprise on enterprise accounts. This enables third-party integrations for enterprise management scenarios.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot impact dashboard adds a return on investment section
item.description:
The Copilot impact dashboard now includes a “Potential return on investment” section. It links Copilot spend to pull request output to help estimate ROI.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review effort levels are generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot code review effort levels are now generally available. Lite and Balanced let you choose review depth based on the complexity and risk of the code change.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: “Relates to” issue relationship in public preview and multi-select fields is generally available
item.description:
GitHub added a new public preview issue relationship called “Relates to” for connecting related work, and multi-select fields are now generally available for GitHub Projects.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Secret scanning coverage updates
item.description:
GitHub updated secret scanning coverage by adding more secrets to push protection, onboarding a new secret scanning partner, and including richer metadata in alerts. The post also notes the Secret Scanning Partnership Program now includes Lovable Labs.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Code Quality no longer adds Copilot as a reviewer

Enabling GitHub Code Quality on a repository no longer creates a ruleset that automatically requests GitHub Copilot as a reviewer on pull requests. Existing repositories with that ruleset are affected only if they already have it configured.

item.title: github: MCP allowlists in enterprise managed settings
item.description:
GitHub added enterprise-managed settings to centrally control which MCP servers GitHub Copilot clients can run. Enterprise owners can now use allowedMcpServers and deniedMcpServers to allowlist or block specific MCP servers.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Set pull request limits at the organization level
item.description:
GitHub now supports setting pull request limits at the organization level. These limits control how many open pull requests a user without write access can have.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Kimi K3 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub has resumed rolling out Kimi K3 in GitHub Copilot. The model is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Customize code scanning default setup at scale
item.description:
GitHub added a new repository property, github-codeql-config-file, that lets you apply a custom configuration file to code scanning default setup. This gives you control over how CodeQL runs on repositories at scale.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Retiring the Copilot Billing Preview app
item.description:
GitHub has retired the Copilot Billing Preview app and it is no longer available. Copilot spend can now be reviewed and managed directly in GitHub billing settings.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of GitHub Spark on github.com
item.description:
GitHub Spark will stop accepting new users and new app creation starting August 4, 2026. Existing users can keep using Spark until August 31, 2026.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Customize Dependabot pull request branch names
item.description:
Dependabot now supports custom pull request branch names through new pull-request-branch-name settings in .github/dependabot.yml. You can configure a prefix, maximum length, and separators for segments and words.

item.title: github: Code coverage automatic enablement in Code Quality settings
item.description:
GitHub added a new Code Quality setting that can automatically generate a code coverage workflow with AI. The change is meant to reduce setup time for coverage in repositories.

item.description:

item.title: github: Customize the reasoning level for Copilot cloud agent

GitHub Copilot cloud agent now lets you set the reasoning level for supported models when delegating a task. This gives you control over how much reasoning the agent uses for a request.

item.description:
Enterprise administrators can now apply managed settings using itemized configuration files targeted at enterprise teams. This lets large organizations delegate more specific governance without routing every change through central admins or relying on a single global configuration.

  • Source: GitHub

GitHub changed issue creation restrictions so users with the triage role can now create issues in repositories where issue creation is limited to collaborators only. Previously, only users with write access could create issues under that setting.

GitHub Enterprise Importer now generally supports self-serve migrations from gitlab.com and GitLab Self-Managed to GitHub Enterprise Cloud. The feature is available through GEI and the GitHub CLI.

item.description:
GitHub Copilot will deprecate several models across all Copilot experiences on September 1, 2026. The affected experiences include Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

GitHub has deprecated Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 3 Flash across all Copilot experiences as of July 31, 2026. This includes Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

item.description:
GitHub has added user-based model policy targeting for enterprise teams in public preview. It is available to GitHub Enterprise customers with Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise licenses and lets AI administrators set a baseline policy.

GitHub is introducing a global default enablement policy for generally available Copilot models on Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise plans. New GA models will be enabled by default instead of requiring admins to turn each one on manually.

item.description:

Repository admins can archive pull requests to remove them from public view without deleting them. Archived pull requests are closed and locked.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: REST API endpoints for Visual Studio Subscription management
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Cloud admins can now use REST API endpoints to manage Visual Studio Subscription (VSS) assignments programmatically. The new endpoint returns all VSS assignments for an enterprise, including assignment details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Xcode 27 runner image now in public preview
item.description:
GitHub-hosted macOS runners now support Xcode 27 in public preview, letting you build and test Apple apps against the latest Xcode version. This is an early-access runner image release.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Improvements to secret scanning and public monitoring
item.description:
GitHub rolled out updates to secret scanning and public monitoring. Resend is now a secret scanning partner, and secret scanning can detect new secret types from APIclub.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — June update
item.description:
June 2026’s Visual Studio Copilot update focuses on usage visibility, a new trust layer for MCP servers, and the first C++ scenarios. The post emphasizes controls and clarity rather than new broad functionality.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot for JetBrains expands BYOK capabilities
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains now supports expanded bring-your-own-key (BYOK) customization across all Copilot tiers, with broader model provider flexibility and improved plugin/provider experiences. The update also includes changes to conversational interactions in the IDE.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Code scanning shows AI security detections on pull requests
item.description:
GitHub code scanning now shows AI-powered security detections on pull requests. The feature expands coverage to languages and frameworks not currently supported by CodeQL.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Dependabot version updates introduce default package cooldown
item.description:
Dependabot version updates now use a default package cooldown: it will wait at least three days after a new release appears in the registry before opening a version update pull request. This applies to version updates and delays PR creation for recently published releases.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Security reviews now available in the GitHub Copilot app
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app now supports running security reviews on in-flight code changes with the /security-review slash command. The feature is available in public preview.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Manage secret scanning custom patterns via REST API
item.description:
GitHub now supports managing secret scanning custom patterns through the REST API. The new generally available endpoints let security teams list, create, and edit custom patterns programmatically.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Code Quality license estimate in public preview
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality now shows the number of active committers for repositories across an enterprise, providing an estimate of Code Quality license cost before it is finalized. The feature is in public preview.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Separate SSO and Organizations pages in Settings
item.description:
GitHub split the combined SSO & Organizations page in user settings into two separate pages: SSO and Organizations. The change is intended to make these settings easier to find and manage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.26.0 adds Kotlin 2.4.0 support and AI prompt injection detection
item.description:
CodeQL 2.26.0 adds support for Kotlin 2.4.0 and introduces detection for AI prompt injection issues in code scanning. The release updates the static analysis engine used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Clearer names for secret scanning detector types
item.description:
GitHub is renaming secret scanning detector types to make it clearer how each detector finds secrets. This is a naming-only change.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Per-user states for multi-user budgets in the REST API
item.description:
GitHub REST API now returns per-user progress for multi-user budgets from a single endpoint. This lets clients identify users nearing their limits without making separate requests.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Mobile: Improved filters and sorting for Copilot sessions
item.description:
GitHub Mobile now supports improved filtering and sorting for Copilot sessions. The update is meant to make it easier to find specific sessions as the list grows.

  • Source: GitHub
